Turn operational rating limbs into rating tables

Source: R/read_operational_ratings.R
operational_rating_tables.Rd

Groups the limbs from read_operational_ratings() into one FlodeRatingTable per rating. A rating whose limbs cannot form a valid table is not forced into one and not dropped silently: it is listed in problems with the reason, so a messy export gives you the good ratings and a precise list of the rest.

A rating is rejected, with its reason, when a limb has a missing level or coefficient, when a limb's upper level is not above its lower level, when two limbs share a lower level, or when the limbs are not contiguous (a gap or an overlap between one limb's upper level and the next limb's lower level).

Usage

operational_rating_tables(limbs, group_by = "rating_key")

Arguments

limbs

A data.table from read_operational_ratings(), or any table with lower_level, upper_level, C, a, n and the group_by column.

group_by

Character. The column that identifies one rating. Default "rating_key".

Value

A list of two elements. tables is a named list of FlodeRatingTables, named by the group_by value, with limbs in stage order. problems is a data.table with one row per rejected rating: the group_by value, station_id (when present), n_limbs and reason.

See also

read_operational_ratings(), compare_gaugings_to_rating(), apply_rating().

Examples

limbs <- data.frame(
  rating_key = c("a", "a", "b", "b"),
  lower_level = c(0, 1, 0, 1.5), upper_level = c(1, 3, 1, 3),
  C = 2, a = 0, n = 1.5
)
result <- operational_rating_tables(limbs)
names(result$tables)
#> [1] "a"
result$problems
#>    rating_key station_id n_limbs
#>        <char>     <char>   <int>
#> 1:          b       <NA>       2
#>                                                              reason
#>                                                              <char>
#> 1: limbs are not contiguous: gap of 0.5 m between limb 1 and limb 2
